Synopsis:
The players use a boat to reach the duergar camp. In the middle of the lake, they are confronted by a group of duergar on a raft. Being Drow/Duergar changes the tone of the conversation and makes the persuasion event easier. Having the mark of the Absolute can also make the persuasion event easier.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_DarkLake_RaftEvent.json: Your party is crossing a lake toward a duergar camp when a duergar raiding party on a passing raft, led by Corsair Greymon, stops you and demands to know who you are—he’s expecting someone named Gekh and enforces a standing order that no one crosses until Gekh’s sergeant’s stolen boots are returned. Greymon is suspicious and threatening (he warns interlopers they’ll feed the fishes), so you can try to bluff, bargain, or turn violent; one available action is a scripted shove that can push Greymon into the water. Off‑screen the duergar camp, Gekh/the sergeant, and any companions or prior flags (who you’ve claimed to work for, knowledge of local events) influence how the encounter unfolds. Note: presenting as Drow or duergar, or showing the Mark of the Absolute, makes persuasion attempts easier; posing as a “topsider” or failing checks tends to harden the duergar’s hostility.
- UND_DuergarRaftCaptain_CampIntro.json: You and captain Greymon have just beached on the far shore and found two duergar waiting — both surly, but Morghal especially gruff and hostile. She’s suspicious of Absolutists/“True Souls” yet openly willing to take their coin, and immediately demands a toll (the “True Soul special”) before letting you through. Morghal reports that Nere, a True Soul, is trapped above by a rockfall and sitting on the gold the duergar want; the crew is on edge (there’s mention of Gekh’s corpse, Thrinn’s injured arm, and abused gnome slaves) so violence is a real possibility. Off‑screen arrival and companion reactions have already occurred; Morghal sizes the player up, threatens trouble if the debt isn’t paid, and remains brusque and watchful rather than listless.
- UND_DarkLake_DuergarBoatAtCave.json: Dialogue when clicking on boat in cave to reach Grymforge. Player can stay or cross. This dialogue only appears once player has already been to Grymforge.
- UND_DuergarLoyalPatroller_01.json: You’re standing at a duergar lakeside post where several drow hang from the bridge as a public warning; the on‑scene duergar is armed, patrolling, and bluntly suspicious, saying the drow were trying to infiltrate the settlement and more may be coming. Off‑screen this is a working duergar camp: other warders, enslaved gnomes, and hauling rothe are nearby and the guards are impatient and terse rather than sympathetic. The duergar mentions the “stench of the top‑lands” and a Clan Flameshade connection, and his mood in the excerpts is angry and contemptuous, so expect short, hostile replies and a close physical inspection of you. Past incidents in the area (elevator/checkpoint to the shadow‑cursed top‑lands and a trapped True Soul reported nearby) may be relevant to the guard’s warning and his readiness to clamp down.
- UND_MyconidCircle_ServantDuergar1.json: Player tries speaking with an enthralled duergar. Duergar players get an option to go hostile afterwards.
